title: Gradient rollout: shadow traffic patterns and tiered regional fallback policy
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a gradient (multi-stage) rollout controller that composes canary, A/B, and shadow traffic modes with deterministic routing and a tiered regional fallback policy. This ticket covers the orchestration and routing rules required to safely promote model variants across capacity tiers and regions, plus precise auto-rollback triggers tied to latency, errors, and quality regressions.

Scope:
- Design and implement the Rollout Controller (service) that drives traffic percentages, shadowing toggles, and region-aware failover rules.
- Add compatibility checks upfront (tokenizer, kv-cache shape, attention kernel compatibility) to prevent incompatible variants from receiving live traffic.
- Define a tiered fallback policy so requests can degrade from dedicated/premium pools -> standard pools -> lightweight quantized variant -> static fallback (canned response) based on capacity and SLOs.
- Wire automated rollback rules: latency P99 spike, request error surge, downstream model-quality drop measured by online evals or shadowing mismatch score.
- Expose controls in the Console (rollout page) and provide audit events to the private log store for compliance.

Non-goals: model training/versioning, model packaging pipelines (handled by onboarding).

Risks/Trade-offs:
- Aggressive fallback reduces correctness; we must balance availability vs model fidelity. Default policy will bias toward availability for public-facing endpoints and toward fidelity for enterprise-configured endpoints.
- Shadow traffic increases infra costs; limit default shadow rate to 5% per variant unless explicitly enabled.
- Compatibility checks may block certain quantized artifacts; we will provide automated conversion suggestions rather than silent failures.
acceptance_criteria: Rollout Controller can drive a 3-stage gradient rollout across regions with per-region traffic percentages
Compatibility gate runs pre-flight and rejects clearly incompatible variants with a human-readable reason
Tiered fallback policy enacted automatically when region capacity < configured threshold (e.g., < 15% headroom) and logs substitution decisions

Auto-rollback triggers fire and revert traffic to previous stable variant when latency P99 > baseline + 50ms for 5 minutes OR error rate > 1% for 2 minutes OR shadow-quality-regression > 2% on ground-truth eval set
Console shows rollout timeline, per-region metrics, and a button to pause/abort rollouts; all actions produce audit events
End-to-end tests that simulate region outage and verify requests are rerouted according to tiered policy

notes: Compatibility checks to include: tokenizer hash match, embedding dimension, kv-cache axes shapes, presence/absence of custom ops
Fallback chain proposal: dedicated-pool -> shared-pool (same model family) -> quantized-variant (same weights) -> small-capacity variant (reduced max_tokens) -> static-fallback message
Shadowing policy: by default route 2% sampled traffic as shadow; allow higher % for internal tenants; shadowed responses must be tagged and persisted to shadow store for evaluation
Auto-rollback formula: weighted score combining latency z-score, error-rate delta, and shadow-match delta; threshold tunable per-project
PR checklist: unit tests for RolloutSpec parsing, compatibility gate unit tests, integration test for regional failover (using the chaos harness)
